summary: Real, untried variant of pooler-k-halves-batched-gemm-m65-m256 (own rows 1.063/1.123 paired; selector and profiler machinery worked under a scored submit). Weaker case: the add costs ~2 us (not 1), so the batched GEMM must reach <= ~17.3 us vs 19.3-19.4 today (~11%) from a tile change alone. The prepare-time selector makes a loss safe and readable.
justification: master unpooler verify_16 m=128: torch.mm(x, unpooler_t) under nn_ok, nvjet 128x64 NNT 19.3-19.4 us, row 18.9-19.15, floor 14.64. 128 CTAs of 128x64 over k=4096 pull ~128 MB of x via L2 vs 67 MB weight; 2-batch k=2048 128x128 halves it; L2 limiter plausible, not shown. The add moves 4 MB read / 2 MB write (pooler m=256 analogue 2.1 us); realistic row 18.5-19.3. Sibling at m=128 picked 128x64 (bmm 20.1 vs 19.4 us); at m=256 128x128. Weakest link: an ~11% GEMM speedup from a tile change on the shape where cuBLAS prefers 128x64. Prior (missing field): pooler-k-halves-batched-gemm-m65-m256; difference is real (tile-deficit fix vs x-L2 re-read on a matched tile).
